headline: Boston College ground game overwhelms Georgia in defensive showcase
body: Boston College's ground attack proved decisive on Saturday, with the Eagles grinding out 168 rushing yards to control the line of scrimmage and dictate pace. While Georgia's passing game stayed busy through the air—Giles connecting on 22 completions for 304 yards and three scores—the Eagles' defense bent without breaking, forcing a crucial turnover that shifted momentum late. Bo MacCormick's 10-carry performance anchored a complementary football approach that kept Georgia's pass-heavy offense on its heels for stretches.

The turning point came when Georgia's offense stalled in the fourth quarter after a fumble deep in Boston College territory. That turnover, coupled with the Eagles' methodical clock management through their rushing attack, essentially sealed the game. Georgia managed 285 passing yards but couldn't generate enough chunk plays on the ground to balance the attack. Leavitt's 20-for-28 efficiency and a touchdown pass suggested Boston College's offense merely needed to stay in rhythm rather than chase Georgia through a shootout.

Georgia's defensive unit, led by Wilson's sack, couldn't manufacture consistent stops when it mattered most. Boston College's ability to sustain drives through power running kept Georgia's pass rush from generating critical third-down situations. The Eagles outgained Georgia in total yards by a thin margin, yet controlled the game's complexion through field position and eliminating mistakes. This was a lesson in how complementary football—rush yards, turnover avoidance, and defensive discipline—can neutralize superior passing volume.
turningPoint: Georgia's late-game fumble inside Boston College territory halted any momentum swing and allowed the Eagles to milk clock with their ground game in the final minutes.

unsungHero.name: Davis
unsungHero.why: Davis led all defenders with six tackles and a sack, quietly anchoring the Eagles' pass rush without the fanfare of the player-of-the-game honor.
